feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/operations expertise. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could use tighter achievement framing with more measurable outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression align well for digital strategy/communications leadership roles.  
- Strong credibility: recognizable employers, large-scale Drupal/web migration work, analytics stack, and multimedia leadership all support the profile.  
- Writing is generally professional and clear, with no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add sharper impact metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more outcomes would strengthen impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign results, cost savings).  
- Fix style consistency: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize punctuation in lists (e.g., serial comma use such as “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. versions without it); and consider title casing consistency (“Topline Skills” vs. “Technical + IT”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more concise phrasing, one or two concrete signals of scale, and less repetition of competencies covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Tighten the opening and foreground seniority, e.g.: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations.”
- Add one concrete differentiator from recent roles, such as enterprise web modernization, analytics/governance, or large-scale stakeholder publishing environments.
- Streamline the final sentence to emphasize value: “Translates complex policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused content and coordinated advocacy messaging.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- Avoid listing too many channels here; work experience already provides that detail.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized higher-value, distinctive capabilities and used more consistent phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize terms: use parallel noun phrases and prefer “communications” over “communication.”
- Replace broader items with more specific, senior-level strengths tied to recent work.
- Consider this rewrite: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS administration & web operations • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional alignment • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, prioritize the most marketable recent strengths: platform modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “policy & advocacy communication” repeat the header and Soft Skills.
- “Web & CMS administration,” analytics, and multimedia are already covered in more detail under Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground outcomes, especially where this role extends beyond your NACo experience rather than repeating it.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, strengthening enterprise communications across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets on systems/governance/operations into one results-oriented line: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics and governance practices to improve coordination, publishing consistency and decision-making.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more concise and outcome-focused: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components and member resource hubs/toolkits.”
- Sharpen the differentiator: “Spearheaded an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this item focused on consulting impact and new initiatives.
- The microsite and AI search bullets duplicate Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It can be tighter and more outcome-driven, with clearer emphasis on enterprise ownership and less overlap with earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and sharpen impact bullets: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcomes where possible for channels/analytics/video: growth rates, production volume, reporting adoption, time saved, cost savings, engagement lift, or reduced vendor reliance.
- Combine governance/analytics into business impact language: “Built analytics and publishing governance across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting consistency and cross-department decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” and recurring video/programming overlap with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems built.
- “Built first in-house video studio” may partially echo older multimedia bullets unless framed as a leadership/capacity-building achievement.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level: editorial operations, recurring channels, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcome language where possible: “Launched/expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel and increasing cadence/engagement [add metric if available].”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems point: “Improved editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” closely repeat the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, planning & content design
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “content design” to sound more senior and specific.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this section to scale already proven in experience: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers.
- Keep terminology consistent with recent roles: use “governance,” “operations,” and “enterprise” since those are strongest in 2022–present work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also repeats themes already established in the header and NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. It should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and implementation strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- SharePoint, Power Pages and Airtable-based systems
- AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress secondary, since recent experience is clearly Drupal-led.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” or fold it into workflow automation for cleaner phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, such as “enterprise web modernization” or “large public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the technical section hold the full tool list.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical leadership, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Put the most strategic items first: analytics infrastructure, KPI design, executive/leadership reporting, then tools.
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-support dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, add one stronger outcome-oriented term such as “measurement strategy,” “insight generation,” or “conversion/performance optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool stack elsewhere; use this section for strategic analytics strengths and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and the Technical + IT multimedia tools list. Tighten it to emphasize operational scope and recent leadership-level capability rather than generic production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task list to higher-value capability list, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production
- Livestream and hybrid event operations
- Studio buildout and operations
- PTZ/multi-camera production systems
- Virtual event delivery and technical direction
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the NACo studio achievement.
- “Livestreaming” is too generic; use “Livestream and hybrid event operations” for stronger positioning.
- Keep to 4–5 bullets and use parallel noun phrases.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- Tool-specific detail like PTZ may be better kept only if targeting multimedia-heavy roles; otherwise it can feel narrower than the rest of the CV.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to sharpen relevance and signal depth in the most recent/important platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent platforms: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add level/scope instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider trimming lower-value items if they’re not central to recent work: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**
- If you want more impact, rename the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** and align wording with recent experience in Drupal-led modernization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one list broad and make the other more outcome/scope-oriented.
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent roles and projects, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and align it to recent work by emphasizing tools actually used to ship, automate, and optimize web experiences.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten phrasing to: HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API and tag integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions CI/CD
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier: “for Drupal-based sites” or “for campaign microsites, analytics, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versioning; plain “HTML/CSS” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; either consolidate or make this section more tool-specific
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap with automation/workflow themes in the next item unless framed as CI/CD specifically

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Best upgrade: replace the pure list with a scoped phrase, e.g. “Workflow automation and team operations: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project coordination in Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; collaboration via Slack and Microsoft Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same wording.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations, audience engagement and campaign delivery**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **used to support newsletters and campaigns reaching tens of thousands of public-sector stakeholders**
- Keep platform names only if all were used meaningfully; otherwise drop the least relevant/oldest tool to stay concise

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters reaching tens of thousands” in Work Experience; avoid restating the same outcome here unless you add a distinct angle like segmentation, automation, or campaign delivery
- “Engagement” is vague; if possible, specify **email marketing**, **member communications**, or **marketing automation**

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup rather than impact. Since later NACo roles already cover leadership and video growth, this entry should emphasize foundational team-building, execution, and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily operations across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outcomes if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, email/social performance, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; specify what changed: “standardized publishing workflows,” “improved production turnaround,” or “supported cross-channel content delivery.”
- Consider: “Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- Team guidance/operations language may duplicate later leadership entries; avoid sounding too managerial here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the standout deliverable: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb/outcome, e.g., “produced supporting digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scale: number of episodes, audiences served, or types of projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item anchored in innovation/research + first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating leadership here since stronger management scope appears in 2015–2024 NACo roles.
